To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
2 doses of an HPV-16/HPV-18 AS04-adj. vaccine induced superior HPV-16 and HPV-18 antibody responses compared to 2 or 4 doses of an HPV 6/11/HPV-16-HPV- 18 vaccine in girls 9-14 years of age.
2 doses of a human papillomaviruse (HPV)-6/11/18 vaccine are more immunogenic than 2 doses of an HPV-16/11/16 vaccine and 3 doses of an HPV6/11/6/18 vaccine in 9–14-year old girls.
2 doses of HPV-16-18 AS04-adj. vaccine elicited superior antibody responses compared with 2 doses or 3 doses HPV-6/16/18 in girls aged 11–14 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunogenicity, safety and efficacy of a 2-dose schedule with the AS04-adjuvant HPV-16/ 18 vaccine in young girls.
the development of a new generation of vaccines that can be used to protect against HPV-associated cancer.
the development of a new method for the detection of the HPV-18(2D).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HPV-16-18 vaccine was non-inferiour to the other vaccines.
the HPV-16-18(2D)-AS04-adjuvated vaccine is a better vaccine than the HPV-6-11-16-18 vaccine.
the 2 dose schedule of Cervarix was superior to the 2 and 3 dose schedules of Gardasil.

the 2-dose schedule for HPV16-18 vaccine is more immunogenic than the 2-doses for quadrivalent vaccine and the 3-dose for quadrivalent vaccine.
